GSM, EPI, PPI & Yarn Count: What Actually Matters When Sourcing Greige Fabric?

When sourcing greige fabric, buyers often receive specifications filled with numbers: GSM, yarn count, EPI, PPI, width and more.

But a common mistake is to look at one number and use it as the deciding factor.

A fabric is not defined by GSM alone.

The way a fabric feels, looks and behaves comes from how these specifications work together.

Let's understand the four numbers buyers encounter most often.

What Is GSM?

GSM stands for grams per square metre.

It tells you the weight of the fabric over a standard area.

GSM is useful when comparing fabrics because it gives a consistent way of describing weight.

But it does not tell you everything about the fabric.

For example, a 150 GSM fabric isn't automatically “better” than a 120 GSM fabric.

The appropriate GSM depends on what the fabric is being made for.

GSM should therefore be treated as one part of the specification, not the entire specification.

What Is Yarn Count?

Yarn count indicates the fineness or thickness of the yarn.

For commonly used indirect cotton count systems, a higher number generally indicates a finer yarn.

But again, yarn count alone doesn't tell the whole story.

The same yarn count can produce different fabrics depending on the density, weave and construction used.

What Is EPI?

EPI = Ends Per Inch It indicates the number of warp yarns arranged across one inch of fabric.

What Is PPI?

PPI = Picks Per Inch It indicates the number of weft yarns inserted across one inch.

EPI and PPI together help describe the density and cover of a woven fabric.

So Which One Matters Most?

This is where fabric sourcing gets interesting.

There isn't one universal answer.

Instead, think of the specification as a relationship: Yarn Count + EPI + PPI + Weave + GSM + Width = Fabric Construction Changing one variable can influence the resulting fabric.

For example, two fabrics can have similar GSM but different yarn counts and densities.

They may therefore have noticeably different appearance, handle and performance.

This is why experienced fabric buyers don't compare suppliers based on GSM alone.

Why the Complete Construction Matters

Imagine you receive two quotations: Supplier A: 140 GSM Supplier B: 140 GSM At first glance, they appear identical.

But what if: ● Their yarn counts are different? ● Their EPI/PPI are different? ● Their weave is different? ● Their width is different? ● Their construction has been achieved differently?

The number may be the same while the actual fabric isn't.

A specification needs enough information to define what the buyer is actually asking for.

Industry guides similarly recommend describing woven greige fabric through construction details such as warp/weft count, EPI/PPI, weave, width and composition rather than relying on one number.

What Should Buyers Send a Manufacturer?

When requesting a quote for greige fabric, try to provide as much of the following as possible: Fabric type Composition Yarn count EPI/PPI GSM Width Weave/construction Quantity Approved sample, if available This gives the manufacturer a much clearer starting point.

The Bottom Line

GSM tells you about weight.

Yarn count tells you about the yarn.

EPI and PPI tell you about density.

But the fabric comes from all of them working together.

For anyone sourcing greige fabric in bulk, understanding this relationship can make conversations with manufacturers far more precise and help prevent mismatched expectations.
